qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Exclusive regulated water and wastewater franchise concessions serving 14M people across 14 states with physically unreplicable underground pipe networks. Statutory rate-making provides authorized ROE (~9.5-10.0%) and capital riders (e.g., DSIC) allowing timely cost pass-through for infrastructure modernization. Erosion risks include regulatory lag in general rate cases, emerging environmental remediation mandates (PFAS filtration capex), and public opposition to municipal system acquisitions.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Balance Sheet & Cash Conversion). Premier regulated water utility with an exceptional 30-year unreplicable moat and essential biological demand, but disqualified by the structural capital trap of regulated utilities: capped ROIC of 6.0%, perpetual negative free cash flow due to mandatory pipe and PFAS capex ($3.1B capex vs $2.1B OCF in FY2025), high debt load of $12.8B (11.5x net income), and sub-hurdle interest coverage of 3.1x requiring continuous external capital access.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 6.0% (2016-2025 range 5.6%-8.4%), constrained by state regulatory rate-base mechanics. Capital expenditures have exceeded operating cash flow in every single year over the last decade (FY2025 capex of $3,126M vs OCF of $2,059M, producing -$1,067M in free cash flow). Long-term debt expanded from $6.3B in 2016 to $12.8B in 2025 ($16B+ total debt). TTM interest expense of $615M against EBIT of $1,879M yields interest coverage of 3.06x (below the 5.0x Munger threshold). Despite holding a solid 'A' credit rating from S&P, AWK's heavy infrastructure replacement cycle necessitates constant reliance on debt and equity capital markets.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
